name: issue_827_recovery_margin_prevents_sawtooth
description: Hysteresis (anti-sawtooth) scenario, rewritten for Design D nearest-edge arming (Issue #1066, docs/08 section 6f; the #827 recovery-margin machinery it originally asserted is retired). Mild day, band 68F/74F, arming margin 2F (comfort_deadband_mild_f): heat is armed at indoor <= 70F, cool at indoor >= 72F, and 71F keeps whatever the thermostat is already doing. Readings that oscillate 70/71/70/71 inside the gap must NOT chatter the commanded mode; the mode changes only when indoor reaches an arming boundary, and a boundary reading inside the 600 s dwell window after a switch is held (locked out) rather than flipping the thermostat straight back.
source: Issue #827 sawtooth-prevention intent, re-expressed for Issue #1066 Design D (nearest-edge arming with hysteresis memory instead of a recovery margin)
notes: Rewritten for Issue #1066: the original scenario asserted the retired against-grain recovery margin (floor + deadband, 90 s sustain, native-family revert). That machinery is deleted. The intent it protected - no heat/cool sawtooth when indoor hovers near the floor - is now provided by (1) the strictly-between hysteresis rule (inside the gap the thermostat keeps its CURRENT mode) and (2) the 600 s dwell lock on non-breach switches.
Occupant impact: a house hovering in the middle of the comfort band must not hear the furnace and the AC trade places every few minutes.

Timeline (floor 68, ceiling 74, m=2): 08:00 indoor 69 -> heat. 08:10-08:25 readings 70, 71, 70, 71 stay in the heat zone / gap -> still heat. 08:40 reading 72 reaches ceiling-m -> cool (first legitimate boundary flip). 08:44 reading 70 reaches floor+m only 4 minutes later -> held by the 600 s dwell lock. 08:45-08:55 readings 71, 72, 71 -> stay cool. 09:10 reading 70 (30 minutes after the cool switch) -> heat. 09:15 reading 71 -> gap, stays heat. Exactly two genuine mode changes after the initial heat arm.

(a) Scenario effectiveness: on origin/main a mild day is natively cooling and heat is the against-grain direction, which required a floor breach beyond the deadband plus a 90 s sustain; indoor never goes below 68F here, so none of the heat switches asserted (or the cool/heat boundary flips at 72F/70F) would occur there. If the hysteresis memory were removed (re-deriving the edge from the day type inside the gap), the 71F readings would flip the mode and the 09:15 comfort_family=heating and 09:10 switch assertions would diverge. If the dwell lock were removed, the 08:44 reading would produce a heating switch instead of a comfort_family_switch_locked_out event.

(b) Docs vs production: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f rule rows 'indoor <= floor + m -> heating', 'indoor >= ceiling - m -> cooling', 'strictly between -> the thermostat's actual current mode', and 'Reactive evaluation, dwell lock, decision memory'.
(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: the HVAC would chatter between heating and cooling while the house sits comfortably mid-band, wasting energy and wearing out equipment.
Classification fields: day_type=mild with hvac_mode=off and windows_recommended=true match classifier.py's derivation for DAY_TYPE_MILD.

events.note: Indoor 69F: inside the heat arming zone (<= floor+m = 70F). Thermostat is already in heat.
Mild-day classification. Selector: 69 <= 70 -> heating; thermostat already heating, so no mode change.
71F: strictly inside the gap (70 < 71 < 72) -> keep the current mode (heat). No chatter.
72F reaches ceiling-m (74-2, inclusive) -> cooling. Non-breach switch; no earlier transition so the dwell lock is not holding.
70F reaches floor+m -> selector wants heat, but this is a non-breach switch 4 minutes (240 s < 600 s) after the last transition: held by the dwell lock.

Scheduled classification cycle at 08:44 re-runs the selector with indoor 70F: heating is wanted but the dwell lock holds it (comfort_family_switch_locked_out). The reactive temperature path itself stays silent while the lock would block, so the lock event is emitted by this full cycle.
71F back in the gap: keep cool (hysteresis memory).
70F reaches floor+m, 30 minutes after the cool switch (>600 s): dwell lock expired, heat is armed.
71F gap: stay heat, no flip back to cool.

assertions.reason: Indoor 72F = ceiling(74) - m(2) arms cooling on the boundary reading. Proves the mode only changes at the arming boundary, not inside the 70-72F gap where four earlier readings left it in heat.
A non-breach flip 240 s after the last transition is held by the 600 s dwell lock instead of flipping the thermostat straight back to heat (the anti-sawtooth guard).
After the dwell window has elapsed, indoor 70F = floor(68) + m(2) re-arms heat before the floor is reached; a non-breach switch.
Final state: a 71F reading inside the gap keeps the family heating (hysteresis memory), not the day-type default (cooling).
The last commanded HVAC mode is heat.
After the 09:10 heat arm no cool command is issued for the 71F gap reading: the thermostat does not sawtooth back.

verdict.summary: Readings that oscillate inside the 70-72F hysteresis gap never change the commanded mode; the mode flips only at the arming boundaries, and a boundary flip inside the 600 s dwell window is held.
verdict.observed_behavior: Heat is held through 70/71/70/71, cool is armed at 72, a 70F reading four minutes later is locked out, cool holds through 71/72/71, heat is re-armed at 70 after 30 minutes, and the 71F reading afterwards leaves it in heat.
verdict.expected_behavior: Nearest-edge arming with hysteresis memory and a non-breach dwell lock never chatters between heat and cool for readings inside the gap (docs/08 section 6f).
